## Detailed description

### 1. External monitors connected, laptop lid closed — WORKING

I use my Macbook with two external monitors connected through a Thunderbolt dock. The laptop lid is closed (clamshell mode). At this point, Ice works normally.

### 2. External monitors disconnected, laptop lid open — STILL WORKING

If I open the laptop after I disconnect it from the external-monitor setup. Ice continues working normally.

### 3. Back with external monitors reconnected, laptop lid closed — NOT WORKING

If I reconnect the laptop to the external-monitor setup and return to clamshell mode, **this is when the problem appears.** Clicking Ice’s arrow no longer hides or reveals the menu-bar items as expected.

I completely quit Ice and reopen it without changing the display setup. The problem remains. Restarting Ice does not restore hide/show functionality.

## Expected behavior

Ice should continue hiding and revealing the configured items after I reconnect the external monitors and return to clamshell mode.

## Environment

- **Ice:** 0.11.24 (build 1132)
- **macOS:** 27.0 (26A428)
- **Dock:** Lenovo ThinkPad Thunderbolt 3 Dock

issue.body:
### Check Existing Issues

- [X] I have checked existing issues, and this issue is not a duplicate

### Description

In an extended desktop layout with multiple displays, with the menu bar only shown on the main display, Ice interferes with right-clicking on the title bar of document windows on secondary displays when the title bar is near the top of the display.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Mac so that it has several displays in an extended desktop layout, with the menu bar ONLY visible on one of the displays (i.e. "Displays have separate Spaces" is OFF).

3. Right-click on document name in title. 

In addition to displaying the path to the document file in a popup, as expected, right-clicking also causes another popup menu to appear with Ice-related options. See screenshot. It's like Ice thinks that the menu bar is there, when it's not.

0.11.11

14.7

issue.title: Zoomed-in part of the screen sometimes jumps around when macOS Display Zoom is active (while running Ice)
issue.body:
### Check Existing Issues

- [X] I have checked existing issues, and this issue is not a duplicate

### Description

Yesterday, I switched from _The App That Shall Not Be Named_ to Ice, and I'm really happy overall. It has all the functionality I need and feels much snappier, especially when using the Search Menu Bar Items feature.

However, there's one issue that is quite problematic for me, related to the Display Zoom functionality in macOS. I have a visual impairment and rely heavily on this feature (Ctrl + / - or Ctrl + Mousewheel). I noticed that when Ice is active and my screen is zoomed in, the mouse pointer sometimes jumps to the top left corner of the screen and back, but this changes the position of the zoomed in portion of the screen (which is quite jarring). 

I assume this is related to screen recording or the rearrangement of icons, and actually, I remember reporting this bug to the developers of _That Other App_ in the past, and they were so kind to fix it. The solution was quite simple, I remember: whenever Display Zoom is active, the code causing the cursor to momentarily move the cursor to the menu bar (and back) is simply temporarily disabled. 

Maybe you could consider implementing such a feature in Ice too? I would love that.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Activate `Zoom` in `System Settings` under `Accessibility`
2. Make sure your screen is zoomed in. It doesn't matter what the zoom level is. But the effect is more jarring. The higher the zoom factor.
3. Make sure ice has something to do. I'm not sure what ice makes do its magic, so I have added screenshots of my general and advanced settings.
4. Just use your Mac for a while. It's gonna be really hard to trigger. And I'm sorry but I cannot really tell you when exactly it happens.


### Ice Version

0.11.12

15.2 (24C101)

issue.body: ### Search for Similar Reports - [x] I have searched existing issues for similar reports ### Description I am experiencing two distinct UI issues regarding the menu bar when using my MacBook Air with an external 1080p monitor. These issues seem related to display switching and resolution handling. Environment: • Device: MacBook Air M2 • macOS Version: 26.4.1 • Ice Version: 0.11.13-dev.2 • Setup: Built-in display + External 1080p monitor ### Steps to Reproduce Issue 1: Oversized Menu Bar on MacBook Air Screen Behavior: The menu bar on the MacBook Air's built-in display occasionally becomes excessively large (oversized). Steps to Reproduce/Trigger: 1. Switch focus/active windows between the built-in screen and the external screen. 2. The menu bar on the MacBook Air screen grows significantly in size. 3. If I interact with a window (e.g., resizing it), a recording prompt from Ice appears. 4. After the prompt appears, the menu bar returns to its normal size. Issue 2: Persistent Blank Space and Shrunken Bar on External 1080p Screen Behavior A (Persistent Gap): On the external 1080p monitor, there is a long, empty blank space on the left side of the menu bar. This space does not disappear and stays there indefinitely. Behavior B (Scaling Glitch): When moving the mouse cursor from the MacBook screen to the 1080p monitor, the menu bar on the 1080p screen often becomes extremely small (shrunken). ### App Version 0.11.13-dev.2 ### macOS Version 26.4.1 ### Additional Information Recovery: Similar to the first issue, it eventually restores to normal size after a brief moment or interaction, but it is easily reproducible when switching focus between screens. Expected Behavior: • The menu bar should maintain consistent and correct scaling across both displays. • There should be no persistent blank gaps on the left side of the menu bar on external monitors. • Switching focus between displays should not trigger sudden size changes (too large or too small) of the menu bar.

comments.body: Same problem. Same specs, except mine is a Macbook Air M3.

### Likely shared root cause behind several reported issues: the Ice Bar is sized from a different screen than the one it's shown on

It looks like #929, #698, #829, and #825 are all the same bug, and it lines up with @ulope's observation in #825 that it's "related to which screen is focused when activating the bar." Sharing what I found reading the source (commit `11edd39`) in case it saves someone time. Note that this is just a bit of code sleuthing, not something I've confirmed with an instrumented build, so please treat the specifics as a hypothesis.

The reports I've seen so far go many ways: icons too *big* on the laptop (#698), too *small* on the external (#829), intermittent and "fixes itself" (#825). My guess for the reasons for this inconsistency is: the Ice Bar's size comes from **`NSScreen.main`**, but the bar is *displayed* on a screen chosen by a different code path. When those two displays have different backing scale factors (e.g., 2× built-in plus 1× 1080p external), the content gets scaled for the wrong one, and which way it's wrong depends on runtime state, so it flips between too-big and too-small.

In particular, it looks like three different notions of "the screen" exist and can diverge:

1. **Capture / scaling screen**, hardcoded to `NSScreen.main`: `MenuBarItemImageCache.swift:196`, cached at lines 219-220, consumed when sizing icons (`IceBar.swift:393-394`) and row height (`IceBar.swift:264`).
2. **Display screen**, chosen separately in `screenForIceBar` (`MenuBarSection.swift:63-72`).
3. **Where the item windows physically live**, i.e. the active-menu-bar display, which macOS ties to the focused window.

Because `NSScreen.main` follows the **focused window**, and the cache also refreshes on a 3-second timer (`MenuBarItemImageCache.swift:45`), the capture screen can differ from the display screen depending on where your active window is.

**Proposed fix direction (unverified):** make the capture/scaling screen and the display screen the same, by threading `screenForIceBar` through `updateCache()`, `updateCacheWithoutChecks()`, and `createImages(for:screen:)` instead of hardcoding `NSScreen.main`.

I've seen similar multi-display scaling issues in `NSStatusBar`-based menu bar managers, and this pattern — correct scale on primary display, wrong scale on secondary — usually points to one of two things:

1. **`NSWindow.backingScaleFactor` vs. `NSScreen.backingScaleFactor` mismatch**: If the Ice Bar window is created on the primary display's `NSScreen` but positioned on the secondary display, the `backingScaleFactor` of the window stays at the primary display's value. On Apple Silicon Macs with mixed-resolution displays (e.g., built-in Retina @ 2x + external 4K @ 1x or 2x), this produces exactly the "tiny" or "massive" symptom depending on which direction the mismatch goes.

   The fix would be to call `NSWindow.setFrame(_:display:)` with the target screen, or reconfigure the window's `backingScaleFactor` when `NSScreen.screensDidChangeNotification` fires.

2. **`CGImage`-based icon capture at wrong scale**: If Ice captures menu bar icons using `CGWindowListCreateImage` or `CGDisplayCreateImage` and composites them into the Ice Bar overlay, the capture happens at the display's native resolution. If the compositing `CALayer.contentsScale` doesn't match the target display, the rendered icons will be scaled incorrectly on secondary displays.

To help narrow this down — which displays are you using (built-in Retina + external 4K, or two identical externals)? And does the issue persist after unplugging/replugging the secondary display?

If you can collect the output of `NSScreen.screens.map { ($0.localizedName, $0.backingScaleFactor, $0.frame) }` at the moment Ice renders, that would pinpoint which path is wrong.

Thanks for the detailed breakdown — this looks exactly like the mixed-scale case you described.

**Displays:** Built-in Liquid Retina XDR (Apple M5, M-series) + a 16" external (FlipAction16) over USB-C. So it's built-in Retina @ 2x + external @ 1x, not two identical externals.

**Scale factors / config:** I couldn't run the `NSScreen.screens.map` snippet (my Command Line Tools are on an older Swift toolchain than the macOS 26.2 SDK, so swift won't compile right now), but `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType` gives the same picture:

- Built-in (Color LCD, main): Resolution 3024 x 1964 Retina → backingScaleFactor **2.0**
- External (FlipAction16): Resolution 2048 x 1280, "UI Looks like" 2048 x 1280 @ 120Hz, no Retina flag → backingScaleFactor **1.0**

So native == logical on the external (1x) while the built-in is 2x — the exact mismatch direction you flagged.

> Hubstaff.app recreates its NSStatusItem via removeStatusItem/replaceStatusItem on HSAppDelegate, which destroys the item and creates a new one. This resets the macOS-managed position, ignoring the user's Command-drag ordering.

But it does not explain why, when and how Hubstaff.app recreates the menu bar icon.

I asked it to make a patch. Here is its explanation of the patch:
> The fix injects a dylib that swizzles those two methods to use NSStatusItem.visible (hide/show) instead of destroy/create, preserving the item identity and its position.

Here is the objc dylib fix it suggested (it works):

issue.title: [Bug]: Ice Bar fullscreen expansion behaves differently depending on which display contains the active window
issue.body: ### Search for Similar Reports - [x] I have searched existing issues for similar reports ### Description There is an inconsistent fullscreen behavior when using Ice with a dual-display setup. My external monitor is configured as the main/primary display, while the MacBook's built-in display is the secondary display. When an application/window is fullscreen and the active window is on the MacBook display, Ice expands the menu bar with the expected spacing/separation, as shown in Screenshot 3. However, when the active window and cursor are on the external monitor, Ice handles the expanded area differently. The space occupied by the Ice Bar is expanded in an unexpected way, and on the MacBook display the resulting layout becomes continuous with the fullscreen window, without the separation/gap visible in Screenshot 3. The result looks like Screenshot 4. In other words, the same fullscreen setup produces different Ice Bar spacing/layout depending on which display currently contains the active window. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Connect an external monitor to a MacBook. 2. Set the external monitor as the main/primary display. 3. Keep the MacBook display as the secondary display. 4. Open an application in fullscreen. 5. Expand the Ice Bar. 6. First, have the active window/cursor on the MacBook display. 7. Observe the spacing between the Ice Bar/menu bar area and the fullscreen application. - This produces the behavior shown in Screenshot 3. 8. Move the active window/cursor to the external monitor. 9. Expand/use the Ice Bar again. 10. Observe the MacBook display. - The spacing/layout changes to the behavior shown in Screenshot 4. ### App Version 0.11.13-dev.2 ### macOS Version 26.6.1 ### Additional Information **Actual Behavior** - The fullscreen layout of the Ice Bar is dependent on which display contains the active window. - When the active window is on the external monitor, the MacBook display loses the expected separation between the Ice Bar-expanded area and the fullscreen application, producing an incorrect/continuous layout. **Expected Behavior** - The Ice Bar should maintain consistent fullscreen spacing and layout across displays. - The expanded Ice Bar should behave the same way regardless of whether the active window is on the primary external display or the secondary MacBook display.
